{"version":1,"content":"

HOW TO USE

Restores a whole folder of old family photos in one Run: Klein removes the scratches, dust, folds and tears, makes the photo sharp, and gives it natural colors, while the people stay the same. Scan or photograph your old prints, put them in one folder, and let it run.

 Pick your folder

  1. On Load Images from Folder Pixaroma, click Browse and pick your folder, or paste the folder's path into the box.
  2. Click Pick images, then Select all, or click only the pictures you want. The button shows how many are picked.
  3. Press Run once. Leave the Run count at 1: the node sends every picture through by itself, one after the other.

This workflow opens with no folder picked: choose your own folder, or try it first on the demo folder Photos to Restore inside the Media Inputs folder that comes with these workflows.

 A folder inside ComfyUI's own input or output folder works straight away. A folder anywhere else works too, but pick it once with Browse: that is how ComfyUI knows you allowed it.

 Pictures go through in name order. Name them 01_, 02_ and so on if the order matters.

 Change what it fixes

The prompt in 2. what to fix works as it is. Change it when you want something else:

  • Keep it black and white: replace and colorize it with natural, realistic colors with and keep it black and white.
  • Only colorize: Colorize this black and white photo with natural, realistic colors. Keep everything else exactly the same.
  • A strong color cast: add Fix the faded yellow color.

 Writing an edit prompt

  • Say what to CHANGE, as an instruction: Put this product on a marble table, Turn this photo into a watercolor painting.
  • End with what to KEEP: Keep the face exactly the same, Keep the product exactly the same. Klein follows that well.
  • Klein reads the picture you give it, so you do not need to describe what is already there.

 Good to know

  • Klein paints the photo again, so very small faces in a big group can change a little. Look closely at faces you know.
  • A photo with a big missing piece comes back with Klein's best guess there.
  • Seed: Fixed gives the same result each Run, Random a new version. Try a few seeds for a photo that matters.

 Something not working?

Each button opens the answer on the Pixaroma help page.

Folder not approved Save to your own folder Nodes look different from the video

{"version":1,"content":"

WHAT EACH NODE DOES

The colour of a node tells you what kind of node it is. Nothing here needs changing except the blue ones.

 Models to download

Orange. Each one needs a file from the Download Models note.

  • Load Diffusion Model (Flux 2 Klein 9B) - The image model, Flux 2 Klein 9B from Black Forest Labs. It is a fast 4-step model that can make a picture from words AND change a picture you give it.
  • Load CLIP (Qwen 3 8B, reads the prompt) - Reads your prompt and turns the words into something the image model understands.
  • Load VAE (Flux 2) - Turns the finished render into a picture you can see, and a picture into the model's own format.

 The steps you set

Blue, and numbered. These are the only nodes you need to touch.

  • Load Images from Folder Pixaroma (1. your old photos) - Point it at a folder and pick the pictures. Press Run once and it sends every picture through the workflow, one after the other. Its resize is set to Max megapixels 1, so every picture arrives at about 1 megapixel, the size Klein works best at, with its own shape kept. Its width and height go to the blank canvas, so each result has the size of its picture, and filename goes to the save node.
  • Prompt Pixaroma (2. what to fix) - What Klein should fix in every photo. It works for most old photos as it is.
  • Seed Pixaroma (3. random or fixed) - The seed. F (fixed) gives the same result every Run, R (random) a new one each Run.

 The work

Green. They run by themselves.

  • CLIP Text Encode (reads the edit prompt) - Reads the prompt through the text encoder.
  • ConditioningZeroOut (empty negative) - An empty negative prompt. Klein runs at CFG 1, where the negative does nothing, but the KSampler still needs one plugged in.
  • VAE Encode (picture to latent) - Turns your picture into the model's format so Klein can look at it.
  • ReferenceLatent (your picture, positive) - Hands your picture to Klein as the picture to edit. There are two, one for the prompt and one for the empty negative, and both get the same picture.
  • ReferenceLatent (your picture, negative) - Hands your picture to Klein as the picture to edit. There are two, one for the prompt and one for the empty negative, and both get the same picture.
  • Empty Flux 2 Latent (blank canvas) - The blank canvas the picture is painted on, at the size it receives.
  • KSampler (4 steps) - The render: 4 steps, CFG 1, euler, simple, the settings Klein is made for.
  • VAE Decode (latent to picture) - Turns the finished render into a picture.

 The result

Dark red, at the end.

  • Save Image Pixaroma (keeps each photo's name) - Saves each restored photo as PNG into ComfyUI/output/Restored, named like its photo with _restored at the end.

 Readouts

Dark. Nothing to set: they show you what happened.

  • Run Timer - The dark clock above the result shows how long the last Run took.

{"version":1,"content":"

RUN TIMES

Measured on a 24 GB RTX 4090 with this workflow, with the models already loaded. A different card gives different numbers, but the shape holds: the time grows with the number of pictures and their size.

WhatTime
4 photos, 1 MP eachabout 11 s, under 3 s a photo
Each photo you addabout 3 s more

Klein needs 4 steps, so it is fast: about 1.7 s for a 1024 x 1024 picture from a prompt and about 3 s for an edit at 1 megapixel, where it also reads your picture.

 The first Run of the session

The first Run after starting ComfyUI also has to load the models from disk (about 18 GB for Klein and its text encoder), so it takes longer. After that they stay loaded.

 On a 16 GB card

Timed on an RTX 4060 Ti 16 GB with 32 GB of RAM:

  • Klein took about 3 to 6 times as long, about 10 s even for one picture: Klein and its text encoder (17 GB together) do not fit in 16 GB, so parts of them load again on every Run, and a second Run is no faster.
